site.title: Local Government Innovation Scan
site.tagline: A daily horizon scan of ideas and technologies reshaping Australian local government.

digests.posture: Quiet Monday scan — no confirmable new, in-scope innovation signal surfaced in the last 24 hours. The sector's active frontiers (FOGO/circular economy, AI-assisted development assessment, AI workforce/governance, smart communities) stay warm but produced no fresh, in-window council announcement today; the strongest in-scope material was out of window (the Council of Mayors SEQ multi-unit food-scrap recycling trial, dated 1 July) or ongoing background (the NSW AI Solutions Panel / DAISY development-assessment program on the NSW Early Adopter Councils track, the NSW commercial FOGO source-separation mandate in force from 1 July).

Quiet Sunday scan — no confirmable new, in-scope innovation signal surfaced in the last 24 hours. The sector's active frontiers (FOGO/circular economy, AI-assisted development assessment, AI workforce readiness, smart communities) remain warm but produced no fresh, in-window council announcement today; the strongest in-scope material was either out of window (Gannawarra Shire's 10-year Resource Recovery and Waste Management Strategy adopted 6 July; the Mullumbimby Civic Centre battery grant application, 17 July) or ongoing background (the NSW commercial FOGO source-separation mandate in force from 1 July, the NSW AI Solutions Panel / DAISY development-assessment program) rather than a new dated event.

Near-quiet Saturday scan — the AI-governance frontier is diffusing to smaller regional councils, but the day produced only one fresh, in-window, in-scope signal. The circular-economy stream was active this week (a $3.7m WA Recycling Modernisation Fund round to 16 regional/remote councils) but that cluster broke ~22 July, just outside the 24-hour window; the sector's other live frontiers (FOGO, AI-assisted development assessment, smart communities) generated no new dated council event in the last 24 hours.

AI moved from single-council experiment toward sector infrastructure today: MAV and ALGA stood up a National AI Working Group while three Adelaide councils jointly bought a four-year AI partner — two different answers to the same question of how a 538-council sector builds AI capability it cannot build alone. Wollongong supplied the day's world-first, and Saturday's watchlist scan produced real yield.

Catch-up edition (7-day window). The week's clearest, most transferable innovation signal was the 2026 National Awards for Local Government (announced 23 June) — a deep bench of judged, replicable council projects spanning road safety, sustainable housing, resilient asset rebuilds, libraries and workforce — against a backdrop of active but mostly just-out-of-window waste/circular-economy moves.
